title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: OCR scanning of images embedded in Office, archive and PDF files on devices
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, configuration paths, PowerShell command and published OCR requirements are supported. Remove the unverified assurance that identity is unchanged, and qualify the billing summary because another Microsoft page documents included OCR capacity through December 2026.

claims.claim: The change is a Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP OCR feature.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview compliance portal: Data Loss Prevention for endpoints - Optical character recognition (OCR) support for embedded images in endpoint

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to extend endpoint OCR from standalone images to images embedded inside files.
claims.quote: This release will extend OCR support from standalone images (JPEG, JPG, PNG, BMP, TIFF, and PDF) to images embedded inside the following files and file types

claims.claim: The roadmap names XLSX, DOCX and PPTX Office files.
claims.quote: Office files (XLSX, DOCX, PPTX)

claims.claim: The roadmap names zip, rar, 7z and more container formats.
claims.quote: container files (zip, rar, 7z, and more)

claims.claim: The extension includes hybrid PDFs containing images and searchable text.
claims.quote: this this release will support hybrid PDF files containing images and searchable text

claims.claim: Image-only PDFs are already supported.
claims.quote: Image-only PDF files are already supported

claims.where: summary; Cost and licensing: Meter; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Each scanned image counts as a billed transaction, and each PDF page is charged separately.
claims.quote: Each image scanned counts as one transaction. This pricing means that stand-alone images (JPEG, JPG, PNG, BMP, or TIFF) each count as a single transaction. It also means that each page in a PDF file is charged separately.
claims.fix: Replace 'Each scanned image is billed' in the summary with 'OCR is metered per transaction'. Add to Meter: 'Microsoft's promotion page lists 2,500 OCR pages per tenant per month at no charge through December 2026, with excess usage billed; the pricing page still gives June 2026 as the promotion end date.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/documentprocessing/promo-syntex?view=o365-worldwide. This reports the conflicting Microsoft pages without changing the published $0.001 transaction rate.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: OCR generally is optional and must be enabled at tenant level, so tenants without OCR configured do not gain these OCR scans.
claims.quote: OCR scanning is an optional feature that you must enable at the tenant level. After you enable it, select the locations where you want to scan images.

claims.claim: An administrator selects OCR locations and included or excluded groups.
claims.quote: Select the locations where you want to scan images. Select the groups that you want included or excluded from OCR scans.

claims.claim: Windows and macOS devices are documented OCR locations.
claims.quote: You can scan images in Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, Windows, and macOS devices.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Configured OCR extends existing DLP sensitive-information conditions to text found in images.
claims.quote: if you configure the DLP condition content contains sensitive information and include a data classifier such as the Credit Card sensitive information type (SIT), Microsoft Purview scans for credit card numbers in both text and images at all of the chosen locations.

claims.claim: OCR generally makes existing records management policies applicable to image content.
claims.quote: When you configure the OCR settings, Microsoft Purview applies your existing policies for data loss prevention (DLP), records management, and insider risk management (IRM) to images and text-based content.

claims.claim: OCR generally makes existing insider risk management policies applicable to image content.
claims.quote: When you configure the OCR settings, Microsoft Purview applies your existing policies for data loss prevention (DLP), records management, and insider risk management (IRM) to images and text-based content.
